newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH ECOLOGISTS PROTEST OVER POWER PLANT PLAN.
newsitem.headline: CZECH ECOLOGISTS PROTEST OVER POWER PLANT PLAN.

text.p: Environmentalists protested on Friday in front of the Prague headquarters of Czech power firm CEZ against its plan to keep some heavily-polluting power plants open despite earlier promises to close them.

About two dozen protestors from Greenpeace and the Czech Duha (Rainbow) movement, some dressed in anti-chemical outfits and wearing gas masks, set up a model power plant with a three-metre (10 foot) smoking chimney outside the CEZ building.
The activists said CEZ should import electricity rather than prolonging the life of communist-era coal-fired plants in the heavily-polluted northern Czech Republic.

CEZ has announced it would delay closure of some of the plants, or even reopen some already closed blocks due to a much faster then expected increase in demand for electricity. CEZ forecasts demand will rise 6.1 percent this year.
"This winter can be handled in other ways than by running old non-desulphurised blocks... by electricity imports from abroad," Greenpeace and Duha said in a joint statement.
CEZ spokesman Miroslav Novak said imports would have to be agreed in advance and carried through even if the weather did not require them, forcing CEZ to halt its own production.

"Those blocks have the character of a reserve for situations when there is a higher need for electricity than usual," Novak told Reuters. "Two thirds of the northern Czech plants have been desulphurised two years earlier than the law requires us to," he added.
